lead.headline: Circle Secures National Bank Charter as US Crypto Banking Framework Takes Shape
lead.tldr: Circle's federal trust bank approval and the CBDC ban in the housing bill mark the clearest regulatory delineation yet: private stablecoins in, Fed-issued digital dollars out. The signal is a deliberate architecture for crypto-dollarization via regulated private issuers, not public infrastructure.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the stablecoin-banking nexus is becoming the most investable regulatory story of the quarter.

top_signals.title: Housing bill that includes a CBDC ban passed into law without Trump's signature
top_signals.summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act has officially become law, incorporating a critical provision that prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). The bill passed into law without requiring a signature from President Trump.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The CBDC ban removes the existential competitive threat to private stablecoins from a zero-cost Fed alternative, structurally improving the terminal value of regulated issuers like Circle and Tether by eliminating a potential monopolist disintermediator.

top_signals.title: USDC issuer Circle wins final approval for US national trust bank charter20m
top_signals.summary: Circle, the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, has received final approval for a US national trust bank charter. This regulatory milestone allows the company to operate as a federally chartered bank, enhancing its legitimacy and operational capabilities within the US financial system.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A national trust bank charter is not merely a compliance trophy—it enables direct Fed master account access, FDIC-adjacent credibility, and balance-sheet operations that transform USDC from a money-market wrapper into a bankable liability with systemic footprint.

top_signals.title: Circle wins licence for some US banking activities
top_signals.summary: Circle has been granted a license to operate as a trust bank, allowing it to engage in specific US banking activities. This regulatory approval is seen as a significant step for the stablecoin issuer's integration with traditional financial systems.
top_signals.why_it_matters: This license operationalizes the charter into specific banking activities, creating a template for how other stablecoin issuers must navigate the regulatory stack and suggesting first-mover advantages in correspondent relationships and treasury integration.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin bulls Michael Saylor, Adam Back slam BIP-110 Ordinals proposal34m, Bitcoin bulls Michael Saylor, Adam Back slam BIP-110 Ordinals proposalThe ongoing debate comes despite a broad downturn in Ordinals transaction activity over the last two years.
top_signals.summary: Prominent Bitcoin figures Michael Saylor and Adam Back have expressed strong opposition to the BIP-110 proposal regarding Ordinals. The debate centers on the impact of Ordinals on the network, occurring amidst a general decline in Ordinals transaction activity.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Saylor-Back opposition to BIP-110 reveals a persistent fault line in Bitcoin governance between store-of-value purists and any-use-case pragmatists, with declining Ordinals activity suggesting the market is already voting against the proposal's premise rather than its politics.

top_signals.title: Hedera lending protocol Bonzo Lend hit for $9 million after Supra verifier accepts manipulated price update
top_signals.summary: The Hedera-based lending protocol Bonzo Lend suffered a $9 million exploit due to a manipulated price update accepted by a Supra verifier. While most funds were drained, a white hat hacker has claimed approximately $1 million and pledged to return it.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Supra verifier exploit exposes how oracle-dependent protocols inherit security assumptions from middleware layers they do not control, a due-diligence gap that should reprice how investors underwrite 'verified by' claims in lending protocol risk models.

deals.summary: TeraWulf is reportedly seeking a $3.5 billion debt raise to fund the development of a data center linked to AI firm Anthropic. This move signals a strategic pivot or expansion from pure Bitcoin mining into high-performance computing (HPC) and AI infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: Stablecoins May Improve FX Access but Worsen Currency Runs: IMF
on_the_radar.summary: The IMF has released a paper analyzing the impact of dollar-backed stablecoins on foreign exchange markets. While they may improve FX access, the IMF warns they could accelerate currency runs by signaling dollar scarcity to the market.

on_the_radar.title: Robinhood to Launch AI Agent Feature For Crypto Trading
on_the_radar.summary: Robinhood is expanding its AI agent trading capabilities to include cryptocurrency. This feature will allow agentic accounts to execute crypto trades on behalf of users, mirroring its existing functionality for equities and options.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken Plans AI-Powered Trading App Overhaul, CNBC Reports
on_the_radar.summary: Kraken is planning a comprehensive overhaul of its trading application to integrate AI-powered trading agents. This move reflects a broader trend of crypto exchanges and fintech firms adopting artificial intelligence to enhance digital finance services.

on_the_radar.title: Senate Democrats call for hearings into Trump’s ties to crypto amid CLARITY Act discussions16m, Senate Democrats call for hearings into Trump’s ties to crypto amid CLARITY Act discussionsFive senators called for committee hearings to investigate US President Donald Trump’s policies potentially being influenced by crypto funding from United Arab Emirates-linked and other entities.
on_the_radar.summary: Five US Senators are calling for committee hearings to investigate whether President Donald Trump's policies are being influenced by crypto funding. The inquiry specifically focuses on ties to UAE-linked entities and coincides with discussions regarding the CLARITY Act.

on_the_radar.title: SK Hynix’s $26.5 billion US listing brought to Telegram users via xStocks
on_the_radar.summary: Tokenized shares of SK Hynix are now available to users on the Solana blockchain via platforms like Backpack, xStocks, and Ondo Finance. This integration allows Telegram users to access these assets through the xStocks interface.

on_the_radar.title: New Hampshire Council Votes Down $100M Bitcoin Bonds
on_the_radar.summary: The New Hampshire executive council rejected a proposal to issue $100 million in Bitcoin-backed bonds. The vote ended 3-2 against the Business Finance Authority's plan.

on_the_radar.title: Backpack joins race for 24/7 stock markets with tokenized equities21m
on_the_radar.summary: Backpack is entering the tokenized equities market to enable 24/7 trading of stocks. This move aims to merge traditional finance assets with the accessibility and efficiency of blockchain technology.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken to relaunch its mobile app with agentic trading and advise at the center
on_the_radar.summary: Kraken is relaunching its mobile application with a focus on agentic trading. The update will introduce autonomous AI agents capable of monitoring markets, suggesting trades, and executing them for users.

linkedin_post: A lot of people saw Circle's bank charter and filed it under 'regulatory win.' That is the wrong read. The 21st Century ROAD Act simultaneously banned Fed CBDCs. Pair the two: Congress is architecting a private stablecoin rails system, not celebrating a milestone. Circle gets national trust bank status. The Fed is barred from competing. This is a deliberate carve-out. We have underwritten stablecoin infrastructure on the assumption that regulatory arbitrage would compress; what we are seeing is regulatory codification that entrenches first movers. The value proposition is shifting from 'crypto-native payments' to 'bank-adjacent liabilities with direct Fed plumbing.' The market is pricing in compliance costs. I think it is underpricing charter scarcity. Watch how TeraWulf's $3.5B debt raise for Anthropic-linked HPC trades versus pure-play mining comps; that pivot is the same logic—regulated infrastructure, real-world cash flows, crypto optionality secondary. Does the next funding cycle bifurcate between charter-holders and everyone else?
